jobs.description:
Mission Statement

Through the use of social and restorative justice principles, Five Keys provides traditionally underserved communities the opportunity to improve their lives through a focus on the Five Keys: EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT, RECOVERY, FAMILY, COMMUNITY.

Five Keys Overview

Five Keys is a nonprofit organization that operates an extensive network of programs across California. With a presence in 14 counties and over 120 locations, Five Keys focuses on various initiatives aimed at empowering individuals and families to overcome poverty and inequity. The organization's programs encompass a wide range of services, including public charter schools, restorative justice programs in jails and prisons, shelters, permanent supportive housing, and the development of new housing and support programs. At Five Keys, the overarching objective is to uplift individuals and families by providing them with essential resources. This includes education, housing, employment, and the necessary tools to sustain their progress. By offering these fundamental elements, the organization aims to create positive and lasting change in communities, making them better places for everyone.

Our Core Competencies

A well qualified candidate has the capacity to communicate effectively
, collaborate
with others while building positive relationships
, demonstrates strong problem solving skills
, has a dynamic learning mindset
, and remains committed to a high level of cultural and social awareness.
A successful candidate will work well under pressure, observe appropriate boundaries and operate with a high degree of emotional intelligence
.

What It’s Really Like To Join Our Agency…

At Five Keys, culture matters. Culture is at the very core of everything we do and impact on a daily basis. We’ve made a commitment to building an inclusive culture that seeks collaboration over hierarchy to create empowered work teams. We serve vulnerable populations daily and we strive to approach everyone with compassion, patience and a trauma informed approach. We choose to push past discomfort to have difficult conversations to impact the greater good. This allows us the opportunity to collaboratively create an inclusive culture and transform the world around us.

Benefits

We offer very low monthly costs for medical insurance! Dental, vision and life insurance premiums paid by Five Keys and various pre-tax flexible spending accounts and retirement account 403b. Generous time off. Annual reimbursement up to $100 towards gym membership, smoking cessation and weight loss programs. Annual reimbursement up to $50 towards annual athletic event participation and annual massage after 6 months of employment. FREE access to wellness-related apps, Employee Assistance Program and a comprehensive mental health care platform for you and your dependents.

Qualifications

JOB SUMMARY

The Supportive Services Case Coordinator reports to the Director of Rehousing Programs and is accountable for providing housing-focused case management and stabilization services to individuals and families participating in Five Keys’ Rapid Rehousing programs. This position supports participants throughout the housing process, from locating and securing housing through developing the skills, resources, and supports necessary to maintain housing and successfully transition from rental assistance.

The Supportive Services Case Coordinator works directly with participants to develop individualized housing stability plans, navigate landlord and tenant responsibilities, access public benefits and community resources, strengthen income and employment stability, and address barriers that may place housing at risk. The position coordinates closely with landlords, rental assistance providers, community-based organizations, government agencies, and other service partners to connect participants with appropriate resources and promote long-term housing stability. This role is also responsible for maintaining accurate and timely case documentation, participant data, and required reporting in Salesforce, the ONE System, and other Five Keys and city housing department systems, such as the San Francisco Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) systems.

We are looking for someone who insists on maintaining a positive attitude and enjoys supporting a diverse group of people. If this job is for you, you are compassionate, resourceful, organized, and committed to helping people achieve and maintain stable housing. You build trusting relationships while maintaining professional boundaries, approach participants through a person-centered and harm-reduction lens, and are comfortable balancing direct client support, community-based work, documentation, and multiple competing priorities.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Case Management Duties

Conduct thorough assessments of guest's needs, strengths, and challenges
Provide housing navigation support to help participants successfully secure and transition into housing, including identifying and viewing available units, providing accompaniment or transportation as needed, completing housing applications, and obtaining required credit, background, and other eligibility documentation
Educate and support participants in understanding their tenant rights and responsibilities, lease requirements, timely rent payments, effective landlord communication, and strategies for navigating and resolving landlord-tenant concerns or conflicts
Provide support services so that clients may stabilize their living situations, improve their mental and physical health, and increase their independence
Develop case management plans and connect clients with community and government resources to avoid loss of benefits and to increase the likelihood of housing stability
Make referrals and coordinate services that lead to increased housing stability, increased income, job placement assistance, and retention
Collaborate with the rental assistance provider to calculate rental assistance and accurately determine participant rental assistance amounts in accordance with program requirements and applicable guidelines
Support participant’s timely transition from Rapid Rehousing Rental Assistance, while ensuring housing stabilization through the development and implementation of plans that promote financial independence, housing stability, and long-term housing retention
Plan and facilitate group Life Skills sessions that may include, but are not limited to, budgeting, household financial management, housing searches, nutrition, landlord communication, tenants’ rights, health awareness, healthcare navigation, and parenting, as applicable
Maintain accurate documentation of participant feedback and grievances and ensure appropriate protocols are followed for review, response, resolution, and follow-up
Develop and maintain accurate participant records, document case activities, review reports, and compile and analyze data to prepare required summaries, ensuring case files comply with Five Keys case management standards and those of funding agencies such as San Francisco Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH)

Administrative Duties

Ensure timely and accurate entry of participant data, services, and outcomes into required Five Keys and external agency systems, including Salesforce and the HSH Online Navigation and Entry (ONE) System; data may include enrollments, assessments, contacts, units of service, referrals, and case notes
Prepare and securely submit monthly, quarterly, and other required reports on participant activities, services, and outcomes in accordance with Five Keys, HSH, and program reporting requirements.

General Duties

Provide a welcoming and supportive environment for all clients and colleagues
Coordinate with community-based organizations (CBOs), government agencies, and other service providers to connect participants with housing, public benefits, employment services, substance use treatment, and other supportive resources, including coordinating on-site services when appropriate
Provide administrative and operational support for Five Keys Rehousing Programs, including compiling and providing program information, documentation, and other materials requested by Five Keys leadership and administration
Maintain accurate records of participant referrals and service connections in Clarity, Salesforce, and other required systems
Document program protocol violations and critical incidents accurately and promptly, completing and submitting required incident reports in accordance with Five Keys and program procedures
Abide by Five Keys and HSH policies and procedures
Adhere to all Five Keys and HSH policies, procedures, program standards, and applicable requirements
Support quality assurance efforts by monitoring the consistency, accuracy, and effectiveness of housing case management services and ensuring alignment with established program standards
Other duties as assigned

Knowledge And Skills

Knowledge of and practice in applicable recovery models including harm reduction
Ability to interact professionally, respectfully, and effectively with participants, colleagues, community partners, and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences
Ability to maintain a calm, approachable, and professional demeanor while communicating clearly and effectively with participants, colleagues, and program partners
Highly proficiency in Zoom, Microsoft Office, Google Suite,and databases and excellent data entry skills
Demonstrated commitment to professional growth, accountability, continuous learning, and skill development, with the ability to adapt effectively to evolving program needs and work environments
Committed to Five Keys’ mission, vision, and values, with an understanding of and sensitivity to the diverse needs, experiences, and barriers faced by the participants we serve
Ability to maintain strong and appropriate boundaries with personal identifying information when interacting with participants or community or program partners, and while at any site location or community or program partner site
Able to maintain strict confidentiality and take all precautions when handling sensitive information
Exceptional written communication skills; ability to express complex ideas with clarity and precision in written documents
Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to establish rapport, actively listen, and effectively communicate with guests, colleagues, and external stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to learn new skills and processes quickly and adapt effectively to changing priorities, circumstances, and program needs
Strong Organizational skills with the ability to handle multiple deadlines and tasks simultaneously
Advanced problem-solving skills; tactfully address and resolve questions/concerns
Demonstrated experience providing case management services and facilitating groups, workshops, or participant-focused sessions
Demonstrated ability to complete administrative responsibilities accurately, efficiently, and within established deadlines

Education And Work Experience

High school diploma or equivalent required
Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience preferred
Minimum 2 years of successful care coordination/case management experience with homeless and/or young adult populations, or an equivalent combination of experience and education
5 years experience in providing direct service to a similar population is preferred

The Program Manager will be CapMetro’s primary contact for the CapMetro’s Bikeshare Operations and Planning Committee as defined in the Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between CapMetro and the City of Austin.

Program Leadership & Coordination

Serve as CapMetro’s primary coordinator for bicycle initiatives, with a principal focus on the Bikeshare program, collaborating with internal departments and external partners.

Planning, Policy & Program Development

Develop, implement, maintain, and update Bikeshare-related plans, policies, and procedures, including system development and deployment plans, service area plans, and long-range capital improvement plans.

Under the direction of the Manager of Cross-Agency Transit & Mobility Programs, collaborate with the City of Austin Transportation Department and CapMetro’s Bikeshare Operations team to oversee system operations, maintenance, asset management, service balancing, system upgrades, special events, and operational and capital budgeting.

Performance Management & Monitoring

Establish and administer Bikeshare monitoring and oversight plans, including annual oversight plans, monthly performance reporting, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), encompassing bikeshare and related bicycle parking and storage programs.

Funding & Grants

Identify grant and funding opportunities for Bikeshare and related bicycle programs; work with CapMetro’s grants team, the City of Austin, and partners to develop and submit funding applications.

Technology Integration

Coordinate with IT and internal and external stakeholders to advance Bikeshare-related technology, enhance the customer user interface, and improve system integration with CapMetro technology platforms.

Customer Service & Issue Resolution

Respond to abnormal or emergency field situations; troubleshoot operational issues; and investigate, respond to, and resolve customer inquiries and complaints through established processes.

Vendor & Service Provider Coordination

Initiate and conduct regular meetings with service providers and operations staff to communicate trends, issues, and concerns, and to ensure performance targets and program goals are met.

Research & Continuous Improvement

Conduct, evaluate, and implement research related to Bikeshare operations, policy, design, and performance to support continuous improvement of the program.

Qualifications

Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in transit, mobility, bikeshare, municipal government, project management or other related field including two (2) years of experience managing employees or projects.

Ability to motivate others by curating a climate in which employees and partners are driven to succeed.
Excellent writing, communication, presentation and public speaking skills.
A high degree of discretion in judgment and ability to negotiate challenging situations that result in consensus while also delivering optimal solutions which result in the most benefit to CapMetro.

Ability to work flexible hours, evenings, and weekends when necessary.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with a diverse population.

Through the use of social and restorative justice principles, Five Keys provides traditionally underserved communities the opportunity to improve their lives through a focus on the Five Keys: EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT, RECOVERY, FAMILY, COMMUNITY.

Five Keys Overview

Five Keys is a nonprofit organization that operates an extensive network of programs across California. With a presence in 14 counties and over 120 locations, Five Keys focuses on various initiatives aimed at empowering individuals and families to overcome poverty and inequity. The organization's programs encompass a wide range of services, including public charter schools, restorative justice programs in jails and prisons, shelters, permanent supportive housing, and the development of new housing and support programs. At Five Keys, the overarching objective is to uplift individuals and families by providing them with essential resources. .

At Five Keys, culture matters. Culture is at the very core of everything we do and impact on a daily basis. We’ve made a commitment to building an inclusive culture that seeks collaboration over hierarchy to create empowered work teams. We serve vulnerable populations daily and we strive to approach everyone with compassion, patience and a trauma informed approach. Qualifications

JOB SUMMARY

The Supportive Services Case Coordinator reports to the Director of Rehousing Programs and is accountable for providing housing-focused case management and stabilization services to individuals and families participating in Five Keys’ Rapid Rehousing programs. This position supports participants throughout the housing process, from locating and securing housing through developing the skills, resources, and supports necessary to maintain housing and successfully transition from rental assistance.

Departmental Overview

New Student Services (NSS) empowers undergraduate students to succeed and facilitates their transition to UC Berkeley. This process is known as the Golden Bear Experience, which consists of two parts: Before Students Arrive (advising and prep, online) and After Students Arrive (Golden Bear Orientation, and Getting Your Bearings, on campus).

Our Mission

The overarching goals of the Golden Bear Experience are to: welcome new students into UC Berkeley’s scholarly community and lay the foundation for fostering their intellectual identity; create opportunities for participants to gain an understanding of academic requirements; create opportunities for participants to connect with university and college resources, services, and support structures; create opportunities for participants to engage with campus traditions and the range of UC Berkeley’s unique cultural communities; create opportunities for participants to engage with their peers and the broader campus community; and set the path for a lifelong relationship with the campus.

The position will oversee a component of new student transition outside of Golden Bear Orientation. Student transition begins as soon as they accept their office of admission and extends into the first semesters. Golden Bear Orientation plays an integral role in that transition, but must be supported before and after with intention that requires building relationships with many campus partners.

The position assists in Golden Bear Orientation programming, student staff training, and student coordinator supervision. Makes recommendations to management for changes and/or development of new activities/services.

Supervision of Student Staff (Programming Assistants) - 20%

Supervise one (1) to two (2) Student staff.
Directs, designs, instructs, and evaluates partial year recruitment, onboarding and training program.
Programming Assistants will focus on GBO programming development and implementation.

Independently handles individual cases regarding student supervision, and/or oversees limited programs as described below - 15%

Researches, develops, and executes training and curriculum for Orientation Mentor and Orientation Leader recruitment and development.
Work with NSS staff to develop curriculum, co-teach course, evaluate orientation leaders, and prepare them for Golden Bear Orientation.

Develops and maintains relationships with internal and external campus stakeholders - 15%

Develops and maintains relationships with internal and external campus stakeholders critical to program success including liaison with the Dean of Students portfolio, multiple departments within the Division of E&I, Student Affairs Communications, SIS team, Tang Center. Specific relationships will depend on Golden Bear Experience and Golden Bear Orientation responsibilities.

Required Qualifications

Thorough knowledge of student development, advising and counseling techniques.
Thorough knowledge of undergraduate (and parent) orientation and transition programs.
Knowledge of leadership theory.
Curriculum design and teaching experience of an undergraduate course or seminar.
Program management of large campus events for students.
Knowledge of common and/or ability to learn University-specific computer application programs and knowledge of and/or ability to learn University and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.
Thorough knowledge of Student Affairs/Student Life specialization.
Skills in judgment and decision-making, problem solving, identifying measures of system performance and the actions to improve performance.
Ability in problem identification, reasoning.
Ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Knowledge of and/or ability to learn about FERPA.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced level knowledge of student development theory, multicultural competencies, advising and mentoring competencies; emerging research on parents of college students, course design and development, and leadership development and training.

Master’s Degree in related professional field or 5 additional years equivalent experience/training. (Preferred)

The Program Manager, MetroBike is responsible for the overall success of CapMetro’s wide range of bicycle programming efforts and reports to the Manager of Cross-Agency Transit & Mobility Programs.
